ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The primary AML/CFT laws of the Republic of Korea are: (i) the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 6516, as amended; (ii) the Enforcement Decree of the FTRA, Presidential Decree No. 17603, as amended; (iii) the Act on the Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, Act No. 6517, as amended; (iv) the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act, Act No. 5493, as amended; and (v) the Financial Services Commission delegation to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU). Beneficial-owner transparency is implemented through regulated financial institution CDD and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting system; there is no public UBO registry for a yuhan hoesa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar with jurisdiction over the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille state: notarize at the foreign shareholder's local public notary, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority in that state, then deliver directly to the Korean registry or authority. For a non-Apostille state: notarize the document, authenticate it at the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalize it at the Korean embassy or consulate in that state. The Apostille route and consular legalization route are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or ministry responsible for companies in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: original or notarized certificate plus Apostille from the competent authority of the origin state, then direct submission in Korea. Consular path: notarization, authentication by the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Korean embassy or consulate legalization. Use only one path; do not add an Apostille to a document that will undergo consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or sworn attorney confirming the current consolidated constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the certified copy and attach a Hague Apostille issued by the origin state's competent authority. Consular path: notarize, authenticate at the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then complete Korean consular legalization. The two methods are alternative authentication regimes, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Corporate Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Korean Subsidiary Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, before a public notary or equivalent competent official
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarized Board Resolution/PoA plus Apostille from the competent authority of the origin state. Consular path: notarized Board Resolution/PoA plus origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication plus Korean consular legalization. Never use both an Apostille and consular legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed regulated bank in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: bank letter notarized and apostilled by the designated competent authority of the origin state. Consular path: bank letter notarized, authenticated by the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate. These paths are exclusive; apply only the one dictated by the origin state's membership in the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copies of Passports of Each Ultimate Beneficial Owner and Appointed Director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary public, embassy, or qualified attorney certifying against the original passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: passport copies notarized and apostilled in the origin state, then submitted in Korea. Consular path: notarized passport copies authenticated by the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs and legalized at the Korean embassy or consulate. The service member states follow Apostille only and non-member states follow consular legalization only; the two routes must not be layered.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding any shareholder, director, or counterparty, counsel must screen the natural-person UBO (25% or more), directors, authorized signatories, foreign parent company, and material business partners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the Korean FIU high-risk and financial-sanctions notices, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, and Korean government administrative measures. PEP status must be verified through commercial databases and public sources for politically exposed persons and their close associates and family members. Findings must be documented in a written risk memo; hits require escalation to the AML compliance committee; false negatives must be reduced by name-alias matching, date-of-birth verification, country-of-citizenship flags, negative news checks, and refreshed screening at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-REG Online Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Hangeul script; Latin characters may appear only as an ancillary trade name and cannot replace the registered Korean legal name. For this entity, the legal form suffix must be Yuhan Hoesa (the Korean statutory equivalent of the limited liability company) and the full registered name must follow the four-tier naming structure: (1) distinctive element; (2) corporate-object descriptor; (3) industry-specific identifier; and (4) the mandatory legal-form suffix. Foreign-language business names must be phonetically transliterated into Hangeul and must match the Articles of Association, the shareholder register, and the Certificate of Incorporation; inconsistent transliteration will be rejected by the registry officer.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the statutory appeal period prescribed by Korean registration procedure, the applicant must file a written objection with the competent District Court registration office, attaching the rejection notice, the legal grounds for objection, and a corrected name declaration through the I-REG online registry. If the court declines to reverse the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. In parallel, the applicant is strongly advised to submit an amended name with the same incorporation application because this administrative path is usually faster than an appeal and reduces risk of conversion into a jusik hoesa while preserving the intended LLC form.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible in Korea only as a correspondence address, not as the sole registered office for this industry. For ISIC 4632 cold-chain keg wholesale and export of craft beer, the National Tax Service and the local liquor licensing authority require a physical place of business, a disclosed or leased cold-chain storage facility, temperature-control records, and demonstrable commercial substance. Korean banks will reject a virtual-office-only address for a corporate operating account and will request the registered lease, utility invoices, site photographs, logistics contracts, and evidence of an on-site manager. Therefore, a virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary registered correspondence address if a licensed and physically operational cold-chain facility is separately established and disclosed to the tax office; otherwise the liquor wholesale license application and corporate bank account opening will be denied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is MODERATE-HIGH for a newly incorporated alcohol wholesaler. The inspection checklist must include: (i) physical presence and signage at the registered office; (ii) documented legal right to use the premises; (iii) cold-chain warehouse lease or third-party logistics agreement; (iv) temperature monitoring and HACCP or equivalent records; (v) liquor inventory, tax invoices, and customs export documentation; (vi) statutory books, shareholder register, and board minutes; and (vii) availability of an on-site manager. Quantified risk: 5-10% annualized probability for a fully compliant company with a real physical office and licensed warehouse; 25-40% for a newly formed alcohol distributor without prior license history; and 70-80% if the registered address is only a virtual office or if the tax office flags the address as a mass-registration address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Chapter V of Part III on Limited Liability Companies, Articles 543 through 613; Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act; Commercial Registration Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (www.iros.go.kr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, in the form prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. Every member contribution must be fully paid or fully delivered before the registration application is filed. Cash contributions must be supported by a bank credit confirmation; in-kind contributions must be valued by a court-appointed examiner under Article 548 of the Commercial Act unless a valid alternative method is provided in the Articles of Incorporation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Customs clearance is administered by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS electronic single-window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity carrying on domestic business through a Korean place of business (including a Yuhan Hoesa subsidiary or branch) must file taxpayer registration with the competent NTS regional tax office or through HomeTax within 20 days of domestic business commencement. The SOP requires the foreign entity to provide its home-jurisdiction corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, a board resolution approving Korean establishment, a tax representative power of attorney where required, and evidence of the Korean place of business. For the Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa, completion of Commercial Registration Court filing automatically triggers NTS assignment of the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the corporate TIN, VAT registration number, and e-tax invoice identification number. NTS subsequently enrolls the entity in HomeTax and issues the business registration certificate. A foreign non-resident entity with no Korean permanent establishment does not require a Korean BRN merely to export commodities into Korea; the Korean exporter substantiates zero-rated exports with its own BRN and customs export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (no US-style check-the-box or pass-through election for a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa). The entity is automatically taxed as a domestic corporation on worldwide income. A 100% domestic parent-subsidiary group may elect consolidated corporate income tax treatment under the Corporate Tax Act with NTS approval; there is no separate election for indirect tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold for compulsory VAT registration once a business location or taxable supply exists in Korea; the reduced-compliance simplified taxpayer threshold is KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable supplies, after which general registered taxpayer status applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through HomeTax and transmit invoice data to NTS no later than the day after issuance. Korea does not operate real-time per-invoice fiscal clearance or a public digital stamping server; instead the NTS e-tax invoice system performs anti-fraud data matching, mandatory electronic signature verification, and periodic VAT return reconciliation. Failure to transmit or issuance of unmatchable e-tax invoices can block input VAT credits and trigger additional tax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim the 0% export VAT rate, the Yuhan Hoesa must supply goods (artisanal hazy IPA kegs) to a foreign buyer, move the goods out of Korea to a foreign customs territory under a Korea Customs Service export declaration, and retain proof of actual export and receipt of sale proceeds. Offshore services or services performed entirely outside Korea are also zero-rated under the Value-Added Tax Act; domestic cold-chain wholesale to Korean retailers remains standard-rated at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export clearance confirmation) filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical carriage from Korea to foreign destination
Export Settlement Confirmation issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank (inward remittance certificate / FIRC-equivalent evidencing receipt of export proceeds)
Commercial invoice and signed packing list for the keg beer export, aligned to the customs export declaration and e-tax invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match export declarations, e-tax invoices, customs values, and bank settlement records to detect fictitious exports. If a zero-rated export is not substantiated by valid export documentation or proceeds are not repatriated within the required 180-day foreign exchange settlement window, NTS reclassifies the supply as domestic taxable, assesses 10% VAT plus interest, and imposes additional taxes under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including refund clawback and, for fraudulent claims, additional tax up to 100% of the amount involved and criminal liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), serving as the Republic of Korea's central bank and principal foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, in coordinated oversight with the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly liberal current-account and capital-account foreign exchange regime. Korean won is convertible with transaction-level monitoring rather than central-bank pre-approval for ordinary trade and operational payments. Craft beer import/export settlement, freight charges, insurance, commissions, royalties, and distributor payments can be executed through authorized domestic foreign exchange banks using statutory declarations. For capital-account transactions such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and cross-border borrowing, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act impose mandatory reporting, but do not impose blanket prohibitions. Exporters are not forced to surrender export proceeds; they may retain foreign currency in a depository foreign-currency account or convert it to Korean won. Profit remittance obstacles are limited to standard compliance evidence: audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, board resolutions approving dividends, evidence of statutory surplus, and verification that the remitted earnings were generated by legally declared business operations. The principal practical friction for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in alcoholic beverage distribution is documentary: liquor-related licenses, customs declarations, and the bank's AML/KYC insistence on proving beneficial ownership and economic substance. There is no surrender ratio that would impair treasury planning, and no material hurdle to opening multi-currency accounts with a top-tier domestic bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must generally be received within six months from the date of export declaration unless a longer period is approved through the foreign exchange bank or BOK. There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account or sell it to an authorized bank at market rates, so the statutory surrender rate is zero percent. Settlement must be executed through a designated foreign exchange bank and supported by an export declaration, commercial invoice, bill of lading, and foreign exchange payment confirmation, with a mandatory notification/reporting duty to the bank and ultimately the BOK for abnormal delays or non-collection.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI viability is Low/Negligible for mandatory treasury operations. A non-bank fintech EMI without a Korean banking license cannot legally provide local won settlement accounts or act as a primary foreign-exchange counterparty for a Korean registered entity under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Such platforms can only be used as secondary payment facilitators or invoicing tools when they route through a licensed Korean bank or authorized payment gateway, and they cannot replace a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank account for capital escrow, export proceeds, or corporate treasury. The compliance recommendation is to avoid reliance on any foreign EMI for settlement and to keep all clearing, capital verification, and tax-related payment records within the domestic banking system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for the statutory representative director or an assigned signatory/authorized officer for initial corporate account opening at Tier-1 Korean banks. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally recognized as a full substitute for face-to-face KYC; a consular notarization or apostilled power of attorney can support the documentary package but does not eliminate the need for an in-person identity verification interview of at least one director or high-level officer at a domestic branch. Independent third parties such as accountants or lawyers may deliver the application, but biometric presence and real-time verification are normally required for the corporate signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the beneficial owners listed on the Foreign Investment Report (FIR), the corporate registry extract for the Yuhan Hoesa, and the ultimate shareholder list of the foreign parent holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Korean corporate registration certificate, full organizational chart with all natural-person shareholders above 15% ownership, passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner, signed beneficial ownership declaration, Foreign Investment Report filing receipt from the foreign exchange bank, notarized articles of incorporation, and a board resolution confirming the source and route of the initial capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Craft beer distribution without a verifiable liquor wholesale license or customs alcohol permit, which raises a red flag under the Liquor Tax Act and Food Sanitation Act and creates concern about the legality of the underlying commercial cash flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Liquor wholesale license issued by the competent local tax office, food business permit for alcoholic beverage storage and distribution, import or export customs broker registration, Incheon/Gimhae customs clearance records, valid brewery/vendor contracts, tax invoices for prior purchases, and a two-year history of compliance filings with the Korea Customs Service and National Tax Service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping indicator: payments to an overseas brewery followed by unusually fast repayment or dividend remittance to the same or related parties, which may be interpreted as disguised capital outflow or abusive profit repatriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed international master distribution agreement, commercial invoices and purchase orders in the transaction currency, bills of lading/airway bills, customs declarations, import/export reports, external warehouse or cold-chain storage contracts, transfer pricing documentation showing arm's-length margins, and bank statements demonstrating real trade settlement rather than circular flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of initial capital, particularly funds sourced from crypto exchanges, cash-heavy trading platforms, or high-risk jurisdictions with no connection to the beer supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month source-of-wealth bank statements from the investor, verified cryptocurrency-to-fiat conversion reports if any digital-asset liquidity has been used, loan-and-borrowing registration with BOK if shareholder loans are part of the capital structure, KOTRA or foreign-exchange-bank FDI approval/certificate, sworn affidavit explaining the full funding pathway, and a negative sanctions match for all counterparties and banks in the remittance chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection into the Yuhan Hoesa must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. If the investor is a foreign national or foreign company, the investment must first be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the foreign exchange bank or KOTRA, and the bank will issue a foreign investment report certificate. Wire transfers should use the Foreign Direct Investment purpose code and arrive in USD/KRW into a dedicated foreign currency or escrow account in the company's name. The bank will verify the remitting bank, the declared investor name, the FDI report number, and the transaction description. Upon receipt, the funds are converted to KRW or maintained as designated foreign currency, and a capital verification certificate is issued only after the bank confirms the funds are irrevocably credited and the statutory declaration is complete.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International trade settlements should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 for high-value direct account transfers, documentary collections for regular repeating keg shipments, and commercial letters of credit for large or transaction-heavy cold-chain purchases where payment security is required. Domestic distributor payments and local logistics should use Korean won wire transfers or local direct debit rails. All outbound foreign-currency payments must be processed through an authorized foreign exchange bank with a statutory purchase declaration, underlying invoice or contract, and customs declaration numbers for the related import/export transactions. The Korean won leg of the clearing operation should remain within local Tier-1 clearing rails to ensure timely settlement and preserve a complete audit trail for National Tax Service and Financial Supervisory Service reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contract with an authorized foreign exchange bank, strictly tied to documented import/export trade exposure
FX swap transaction for rolling short-term KRW/USD settlement exposure
Cross-currency swap between KRW and USD only when supported by a long-term underlying commercial or financing contract
FX option or collar structure purchased from a licensed bank to hedge future craft beer trade receivables/payables
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) through a properly authorized domestic bank or offshore branch, limited to hedging actual Korean-won cash flows and never used for speculative uncovered positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return for Yuhan Hoesa (including Local Income Tax Surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, submitted through the HomeTax electronic system; Local Income Tax surtax remitted to the competent local government through NTS-integrated local tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the filing deadline is 31 March, automatically extended to 30 April when the company is subject to a statutory external audit or uses the tax-return extension available under the Framework Act on National Taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; under-reporting penalty of 10% of the understated tax amount; late-payment surcharge calculated at 0.03% per day on arrears from the statutory due date; persistent failure to file for six consecutive business years may result in administrative cancellation of the business registration by the NTS, tax seizure, and court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Regular Meeting of Members (Annual General Meeting of the Yuhan Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory books at the registered office (Register of Minutes and financial statements); no government filing is required for a non-listed, non-externally-audited LLC unless audited financial statements are filed with the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular members' meeting must be convened within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company the meeting and approval of financial statements must be completed by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors failing to convene the regular meeting are subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,500) under the Commercial Act; unresolved omissions may also be used as evidence of failure to maintain statutory books and could prejudice owner claims to limited liability and require shareholder indemnification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report (Independent Certified Public Accountant's Opinion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) of South Korea through the e-Audit external auditor reporting system, with a copy to the National Tax Service if the audit is used for the 30 April corporate income tax filing extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor must deliver the audit report to the company and file the report with the FSS within two weeks after the auditor's delivery date, and in all cases before the regular meeting of members (31 March for a calendar-year company) and before the 30 April tax return deadline when the audited financial statements are used
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo a mandatory external audit may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 37,500); the auditor's registration may be suspended for non-filing with the FSS; NTS may reject the corporate income tax return as defective if audited financial statements are required and absent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return and Tax Invoice Matching Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual calendar-year VAT periods: first semester (January 1 to June 30) filed by July 25; second semester (July 1 to December 31) filed by January 25 of the following year; if the due date falls on a non-business day, the deadline moves to the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled VAT return attracts 20% of the unpaid VAT as a non-filing penalty; failure to issue or receive valid tax invoices may attract up to 2% of the supply value in penalties; daily late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.03% on overdue VAT; repeated non-filing can trigger business registration cancellation and tax office seizure measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Maintenance and NTS Registered Address Verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Tax Office (National Tax Service); change-of-address registration through NTS HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual renewal is required; however, any change in the registered office, representative, business description, or foreign ownership status must be reported to the NTS within 30 days of the event; an annual registered-office diligence check should be completed by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a change notice may trigger a negligence penalty of up to KRW 1 million (approximately USD 750); failure to maintain an actual operational registered office can lead to cancellation of the business registration by the district tax office, and the Korean court may treat the LLC as administratively extinct if it has no registered office and no statutory management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Corporate Registers and Ultimate Beneficial Ownership / Foreign Investment Status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretarial records at the registered office; for foreign investors, a change report to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the domestic designated agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual internal confirmation completed within 30 days after the regular members' meeting (by 30 April for a calendar-year entity); a statutory 30-day reporting window applies to any transfer of members' interests, changes in directors, changes in foreign ownership proportion, or changes in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, failure to file a change report within 30 days may result in an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,750); incomplete member registers may invalidate a transfer against the company, and directors may be fined up to KRW 10 million for breach of statutory record-keeping duties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liquor Wholesale License Compliance and Alcohol Sales Record Inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Regional Tax Office, National Tax Service (liquor license supervisory section); supporting records held at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No periodic renewal filing is required once the license is issued, but the licensee must retain alcohol purchase/sales records for at least five years and must report any change to the license conditions, equity ownership, or business address to the NTS within 30 days; the records and VAT returns serve as the annual compliance evidence by 25 January for the second VAT semester
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid liquor wholesale license may trigger criminal fines and license forfeiture under the Liquor Tax Act; submission of false sales records can result in a fine of up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 15,000) and cancellation of the liquor license; the NTS may also treat the false records as fraudulent tax reporting with a 40% unjust-return penalty

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Korea's Commercial Act, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered if the Yuhan Hoesa meets any of the following at fiscal year-end: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); (ii) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.25 million) together with total liabilities equal or exceed KRW 7 billion or an annual employee count of 100 or more; (iii) annual turnover equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) regardless of asset size; (iv) the company is otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission as a publicly relevant entity. A licensed liquor wholesaler is not exempted merely by its LLC structure; the thresholds are tested on individual legal-entity financial statements under Korean GAAP. If no threshold is met, the company may still elect a voluntary audit, and any audit must be performed by a CPA firm registered with the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), not an ordinary accountant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for companies listed on a Korean securities exchange and for entities designated by the Financial Services Commission; all other externally audited and non-listed entities may apply K-GAAP (General Purpose Financial Reporting Standards). The Yuhan Hoesa, as a non-listed low-risk beer distribution company that is not a financial institution, will ordinarily use K-GAAP or the Korea SME Accounting Standards. The annual tax-basis closing must be reconciled to K-GAAP/IFRS book financial statements, and all books must be maintained in Korean Won with Korean-language supporting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a central annual UBO filing for private LLCs; therefore the Yuhan Hoesa must internally confirm and update the member register and director register as of each fiscal year-end and complete that confirmation no later than 30 days after the regular members' meeting. Any transfer of members' interests, admission of a new member, resignation or appointment of a director, or change in foreign ownership percentage must be registered in the statutory books and, where the change is made by a foreign investor, reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the effective change. The 30-day reporting window is mandatory for foreign ownership changes; for purely domestic membership changes the company must make a contemporaneous board/member resolution and update the transfer ledger in the register of members, because the transfer is not effective against the company until the register is updated.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,600 per year depending on Seoul/CBD virtual office and corporate secretarial service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a small to mid-capacity wholesale/export distribution LLC; a voluntary review engagement is typically USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 if the statutory audit threshold is not met

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (top national CIT marginal rate for taxable income over KRW 300 billion) plus 2.4% local income tax surcharge = 26.4% aggregate headline rate; for a mid-sized craft beer wholesale LLC the relevant marginal rate is more commonly 9%–21% national plus 0.9%–2.1% local surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory SME tax credits for job creation, facility investment and R&D (up to 50% of qualifying R&D expenditure); no free-zone CIT holiday for ordinary domestic distribution in Korea; the local income tax surcharge equals 10% of the national CIT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 110, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system (hometax.go.kr), together with the Local Income Tax Return (Form No. 210) for the 10% local surcharge.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory filing deadline is 31 March of the following year. A filing extension of up to one month may be granted for foreign audit or overseas operations, but the payment deadline is not extended unless a separate installment payment plan is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Entity Identification and Tax Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation registration number, legal name (Yuhan Hoesa), Korean tax office, industry code (ISIC 4632 / NAICS 424810), fiscal year start and end dates, representative director, and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number of the domestic LLC. If the LLC is 100% foreign-owned, disclose foreign investment in the applicable foreign-invested company schedule. A Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation for Korean CIT purposes and must report worldwide income even if all shareholders are non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach Korean GAAP or K-IFRS financial statements showing revenue from craft beer keg wholesale, cold-chain distribution, inventory, trade receivables, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record revenue when cold-chain delivery is completed and title passes. Include export sales of hazy IPAs and reconcile keg deposits and shrinkage. Non-resident shareholders must ensure the books and records are maintained at the Korean registered office and are available to the National Tax Service in Korean.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of temporary and permanent differences, nondeductible expenses, entertainment expenses, depreciation differences, and disallowed intercompany payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back payments to foreign affiliates that lack economic substance or exceed arm's-length pricing. Royalties for brand or hazy IPA recipe use must be supported by a written licence agreement, and management fees must be recharged at cost with a mark-up only if actually rendered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Taxable Income and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of final taxable income after nontaxable income, deductible losses, and loss carryforward deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct prior-year losses with a 5-year carryforward limit; the loss must be chronologically applied. Losses of a foreign permanent establishment are allowable only while Korea taxes the worldwide income of the Korean domestic corporation. No deduction is allowed for paper losses of a shell affiliate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Tax Computation and Credits / Reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive national CIT rates, compute the 10% local income tax surcharge, and subtract foreign tax credits, R&D credits, and SME investment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the current Korean brackets: 9% on the first KRW 200 million, 19% on the amount exceeding KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, 21% above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion. Local surtax is 10% of national CIT. Foreign dividend gross-up and underlying foreign tax credit claims must be supported by a TRC and dividend distribution documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Final Tax Payable and Prepayment Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT and local surcharge after interim self-assessment, quarterly prepayments, and previously withheld domestic income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is for the Yuhan Hoesa's own CIT. Outbound dividends and royalties to non-resident shareholders are subject to a separate Non-Resident Withholding Tax Return. Do not reduce final CIT by amounts withheld from third parties unless the company is a withholding agent reconciling its own credit position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Non-Resident Transaction Schedules and DTA Relief Forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedules of cross-border payments: dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, and transfer pricing disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the withholding tax statements for remittances to foreign shareholders. Apply the statutory 22% aggregate WHT for dividends, interest, and royalties; if treaty relief is claimed, attach the exemption/reduction application with the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate and Beneficial Ownership Declaration before applying a lower DTA rate. The tax office rejects relief for a conduit without substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Attachments and Transfer Pricing Documentation Index
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Checklist of required attachments: financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, TP summary report, local file, master file, and supporting contracts with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If intercompany transactions exceed KRW 5 billion, prepare and attach the Local File; if group consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, prepare the Master File and Country-by-Country Report. For the craft beer export leg, document comparable wholesale margins and allocation of cold-chain logistics risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax. Unpaid tax also accrues a daily delinquency charge of 0.022% from the day after the statutory deadline until full payment. Fraudulent or willful understatement is penalized at 40% of the evaded tax. Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, criminal prosecution can result in imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million; local income tax surcharge penalties are added on the same base.
